newsitem.title: USA: IMF delays decision on Pakistan loan until Dec. 17.
newsitem.headline: IMF delays decision on Pakistan loan until Dec. 17.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund's board on Friday put off a decision on whether to resume lending to Pakistan until December 17.
An IMF spokesman said in a statement that the board at that time will also consider expanding and extending its outstanding $600 million stand-by loan for the country.
The IMF withheld two $80 million disbursements of the stand-by loan due in June and September because it was unhappy with the performance of the economy and the government's 1996/97 budget plans.
Since then, the country has worked to get back into the IMF's good graces through a series of measures aimed at reforming and stabilizing the economy.
Shahid Javed Burki, an adviser to the Parkistan government, briefed the IMF board on the country's efforts at its informal meeting on Friday, the Fund spokesman said.

Besides agreeing to consider expanding and extending the stand-by loan until September 1997, the board also left open the possibility of negotiating a separate, low-cost loan with the country next year.

"It is understood that the important structural reforms envisaged by the Pakistan authorities for 1997 and beyond could provide a basis for discussion of an ESAF program in 1997," the IMF spokesman said.
ESAF, or the Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility, is an IMF program that lends money to poor countries at just a half percent interest rate.
